title: driver-shim-oom-audit-scratchpad
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for a recurring intermittent OOM / cuInit / libcuda mismatch we've seen on a subset of prod GPU nodes. Goal is to capture commands tried, exact error snippets, quick hypotheses, and minimal repro notes so SRE/infra can triage fast.

Background / symptom summary:
- Multiple tasks (chat model shards, refactor branch) have been failing with either immediate CUDA init errors inside containers or throwing OOMs mid-generation with inconsistent reported VRAM usage.
- Failures are clustered to nodes in rack-3 (nvidia-driver 535.86) and a new kpatch rolled out 2026-02-26.
- Containers built on host A (driver 535) sometimes fail when scheduled onto host B (driver 530) with the same image.

Representative error snippets (copied raw):
1) container startup / cuda init:
   2026-03-05T09:14:33Z ERROR runtime: cuInit(0) failed: unknown error
   runtime: failed to initialize CUDA driver: cuInit returned 999

2) undefined symbol on load:
   python: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: undefined symbol: cuDeviceGetAttribute

3) OOM during generation (trainer process):
   RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 16.00 GiB total capacity; 12.4 GiB already allocated; 1.80 GiB free; 1.16 GiB cached)
   NOTE: free/allocated numbers from pytorch don't always reflect nvml output.

4) NVML mismatch in dmesg:
   [ 1234.567890] NVRM: API mismatch: the client has the 535.86 and the kernel module has 530.41

Commands & quick probes tried (in order):
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION -- showed different driver versions reported inside container vs host on failure nodes.
- docker run --rm --gpus all --env NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility --entrypoint bash IMAGE -c "ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* && strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | head"
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; import os; print(torch._C.__file__)') to check linked libcuda path. Found libcuda symlink pointing to host-provided lib but versions mismatched.
- ldconfig -p | grep libcuda to inspect system cache. On one node ld.so.cache had stale 530 references.
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version and modinfo nvidia to compare kernel module version.
- dmesg | grep NVRM to surface API mismatch messages (see above).
- strace -f -e open,openat -p <pid> on model process during startup to see what lib paths are opened. Observed mixed /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu and /usr/local/cuda/compat links.
- python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')" to provoke symbol lookup errors; reproduced the undefined symbol message when host lib and container runtime were misaligned.

Container / image notes:
- Images are multi-stage, base image includes cuda-toolkit-11.8 (for build), runtime relies on host libcuda; we intentionally do not ship libcuda in image.
- Some developer images accidentally include /usr/local/cuda/lib64 symlink which masks host lib when running with some runtimes.
- Recent change: switched from nvidia-container-runtime v3 -> v4 in Feb; behavior differs when container includes partial CUDA libs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver / kernel module mismatch (API mismatch) after partial driver roll (most likely). dmesg explicitly shows API mismatch. Explanation: module on host still older (530) but userspace libraries updated to 535; result = undefined symbols or cuInit failure.
2) Image ships a partial CUDA userlib (e.g., libcuda.so stub) that gets picked up instead of host-provided library, causing missing symbols or version skew. (Seen in traces where /usr/local/cuda/lib64 present).
3) NVML/driver state corrupted on warm node after long uptime + repeated container loads; only full driver reload solves it.
4) Pytorch caching / fragmentation: allocations grow because of suboptimal caching when kernels differ causing different memory footprints; explains OOM-like numbers that don't match nvml. Less likely for startup cuInit errors.

Interventions attempted / results:
- Reboot node (temp fix): nodes rebooted & all tasks recovered for ~48h, then failures recurred. Suggests kernel module + userlib drift over updates.
- Full driver reinstall (535.86) on one problematic node: fixed immediately. Leaving this node as a canary.
- Forced removal of /usr/local/cuda/lib64 symlink from image and rebuild: some reduction in failures for that image variant.
- Replacing nvidia-container-runtime v4 -> v3 on a test host: inconsistent results; v3 picked host lib more reliably in one case.
- Added preflight check in task runner to run `ldd` on torch._C and ensure libcuda.so resolves to host path; we started failing fast (reject scheduling) if mismatch detected.

Minimal repro notes (how to reproduce locally):
1) Host A: install driver 535 (userspace libs) but don't update kernel module (simulate mismatch) -> modprobe shows 530 kernel module.
2) Build image that does NOT include libcuda but DOES include /usr/local/cuda/lib64 with some compatibility stubs.
3) Run docker with --gpus all and nvidia runtime v4; inside container run "python -c \"import torch; torch.zeros(1).cuda()\"" -> observe cuInit or undefined symbol.

Checklist for next triage run (whoever picks this up):
- [ ] Collect `modinfo nvidia`, `/proc/driver/nvidia/version`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` from host and from within a repro container.
- [ ] Gather `ldd` output of torch._C inside failing container and `readelf -d` on libcuda.so.1 if present.
- [ ] Check `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/` and `ldconfig -v` for stale entries. Snapshot `ld.so.cache`.
- [ ] If dmesg shows API mismatch, escalate to infra to verify recent driver rollout plan and kernel module build status (kernel ABI drift).
- [ ] Try reproducing with singularity / podman to see runtime-specific path munging.
- [ ] Add small regression test: start a container that tries `ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')` and fail-fast if symbol lookup fails; hook into our scheduler pre-scheduling check.

Notes to self / messy other observations:
- Observed one case where `nvidia-smi` inside container reported driver 535 while `modinfo nvidia` on host reported 530 – weird but consistent with partial upgrade where userspace libs were updated but kernel module not yet recompiled.
- A workaround that sometimes helps: set LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 inside container (forces host lib) but it's brittle and not a long-term solution.
- There may be a subtle race with our node updater: it swaps driver rpm files, restarts kubelet, but doesn't always unload old kernel module in time.
- Look at salt/ansible playbook that did driver rollout on 2026-02-26; link: infra playbook PR 924.

Open questions:
- Why do some containers pick up host lib and others pick up image-supplied lib with same runtime? Is it ordering of lib paths vs LD_LIBRARY_PATH set by wrapper?
- Is there a chance that CUDA toolkit packages from apt pull a partial libcuda stub into the image at build time? Need to audit base images.

Immediate action plan (short):
- Add fast-fail preflight in runner to detect libcuda mismatch (already started).
- Schedule canary nodes to fully reinstall kernel module + driver and keep them observation-only for a week.
- Audit a sample of top 10 failing images to see if they ship any CUDA userlibs.
- Make a small doc for devs: "don’t include libcuda in images; if you must, pin fully compatible versions and test against host drivers".

If you pick this up, start by grabbing the node logs at /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and /var/log/dmesg* and ping me (Maya) in #infra-gpu with node name.

-- end of scratchpad --
